Implementation Plan

# Plan: move the polling loops' read calls from `GH_PAT` to the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (issue #9888)

The plan is ready (STATUS: CLEAR). It covers every polling loop that actually calls GitHub. Three facts from the code change what the issue asked for:
- **The two validate loops make no GitHub calls.** `validate_process.sh` only watches a log file's size and `validate_driver.sh` polls Docker health, so neither changes.
- **The release-gate loops need a second copy of the logic.** Their shared read helper (`gh_api_safe`) deliberately does not load `gh_helpers.sh`, so its file is added to the change list.
- **The release gate's polling jobs need read permissions.** Their job token currently has only `contents: write`, so three read scopes are added at the top of `test-and-mark-stable.yml`.

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `cb39aad54210f22041492a5844755dc561a45cb3`, branch `main` (resolved checkout ref `main`). The integration-branch mismatch line reads `unknown`, not `true`, so this plan is not blocked on it.

## Automation (§20.E)
- **New scripts:** none. The change adds `gh_read()` and its helpers to `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`, adds one read helper to `scripts/comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh`, and edits existing scripts and workflow steps.
- **Entry points:** unchanged.
  - `promote-main-to-stable.yml`: schedule, job `cycle`, step "Run the promote cycle".
  - `test-and-mark-stable.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` only, started by `auto-release-stable.yml`.
  - `review_autofix.yml`: PR events, job `codex-agent`.
  - `workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`: jobs `intake` and `recovery-scan`.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none.
- **DB work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry, because no single-use or long-running script is added.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`: add `gh_read()` and private helpers next to `gh_review_pr_state` (line ~1022)

- **Signature:** `gh_read [--same-repo-only] <gh subcommand args…>`, for example `gh_read --same-repo-only api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/1"`.

- **Write-verb refusal** (new private helper `_gh_read_args_are_read`).
  - Allowed:
    - `api` with no method, or `-X` / `--method` set to `GET` or `HEAD` (any case, including the `-XGET` and `--method=GET` forms).
    - Field flags (`-f`, `-F`, `--field`, `--raw-field`) are allowed only together with an explicit `GET`; without a method, `gh` sends a POST.
    - `run view`, `run list`, `pr view`, `pr list`, `pr checks`, `issue view`, `issue list`, `workflow view`, `workflow list`.
  - Refused, with return code 2 and no `gh` call at all:
    - `--input` with any method;
    - the `graphql` endpoint;
    - any other subcommand: `pr merge`, `issue comment`, `workflow run`, `run cancel`, `-X POST`, `-X PATCH`, `-X PUT`, `-X DELETE` and so on.
  - On refusal it prints one stderr line, `gh_read: refused non-read command <summary>`, built with the existing `_gh_cmd_log_summary gh "$@"`. That helper is credential-free and already defuses `::`.
  - The refusal happens before the token selection below, so it applies even when the feature is off. This is the "no write ever goes through `gh_read`" invariant.

- **Plain mode.** It runs `gh "$@"` unchanged (today's behaviour) when any of these holds:
  - `GH_READ_TOKEN` is unset or empty;
  - `GH_READ_TOKEN_ENABLED` (default `true`) is set to `false`, `0`, `no` or `off`, compared case-insensitively;
  - the per-job refusal latch (below) is present.

  Consumers' older stable copies keep working because no workflow there exports `GH_READ_TOKEN`.

- **Same-repo check** (`--same-repo-only`).
  - The target repo comes from the first `repos/<owner>/<repo>/` endpoint of an `api` call (a leading `/` is allowed), or from `-R` / `--repo <owner/repo>` for other subcommands.
  - If it cannot be found, or it differs from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` (case-insensitive), the call goes straight to the PAT (plain `gh "$@"`) without trying the job token and without a log line.

- **Job-token attempt.**
  - Save the xtrace state, then turn xtrace off (`{ set +x; } 2>/dev/null`) so the token can never be echoed.
  - Run `GH_TOKEN="${GH_READ_TOKEN}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${GH_READ_TOKEN}" gh "$@"`, with stdout and stderr captured to `mktemp` files under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`. Restore xtrace afterwards.
  - On success, print the captured stdout, replay stderr and return 0.

- **Fallback on 401, 403, 404 or a rate limit.**
  - These are detected by `HTTP 401` / `HTTP 403` / `HTTP 404` in stderr, or by the existing `_is_gh_rate_limit`.
  - Throw the captured output away (so no half-paginated output reaches the caller), log one stderr line `GH_READ_FALLBACK reason=<401|403|404|rate_limit> caller=<script>`, then run `gh "$@"` once with the caller's own `GH_TOKEN` (the PAT) and return its exit code.
  - `<script>` is `basename "${BASH_SOURCE[1]}"`, cleaned to `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, with `unknown` when empty.
  - The reason token uses an underscore, so the `GH_READ_FALLBACK` line can never match `_is_gh_rate_limit` (`rate limit` with a space) in a wrapping `gh_retry`.

- **Refusal latch.**
  - A 401 or a 403 that is not a rate limit means the token lacks permission, so the function writes a latch file: `${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/gh_read_refused_${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}_${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-1}_${GITHUB_JOB:-job}`.
  - While the latch exists, later calls go straight to the PAT, so a missing scope does not cost a wasted call and a log line on every tick.
  - 404 and rate limits do not latch: a 404 can be a real missing resource, and the rate limit resets.
  - This follows the same pattern as the comment-signing helper's `_refusal_flag` in the same file (line ~690).

- **Other failures** (5xx, network): replay the captured stdout and stderr and return the original exit code with no fallback. Callers' existing retry wrappers (`gh_retry`) handle those as they do today.

- **`gh_review_pr_state`** (the reviewer and editor watchdog read):
  - Change both reads, the no-cache branch and the cache-miss read at line ~1046, from `gh_retry gh api "repos/${repo}/pulls/${number}" --jq .state` to `gh_retry gh_read --same-repo-only api "repos/${repo}/pulls/${number}" --jq .state`.
  - The fallback definitions in `review_run_reviewers.sh:17` and `review_apply_fixes.sh:32` are used only when `gh_helpers.sh` is missing, so they stay unchanged.

### 2. `scripts/comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh`: a self-contained twin
This file says it must not load `gh_helpers.sh` (lines 93–96), so `gh_read` is not available to the release-gate loops.

- **Add `gh_api_safe_job_token_read`** (check the name is unused first). It applies the same rules as `gh_read`:
  - reads only (reusing the file's existing `gh_api_safe_call_is_read`);
  - same repo only, judged from the endpoint;
  - the same plain mode and kill switch;
  - the same latch file name;
  - xtrace off around the token;
  - the same `GH_READ_FALLBACK reason=… caller=…` line.

  It returns 0 with output on success and a distinct code (3) for "fall back to the PAT".

- **Change `gh_api_safe`.** When the new opt-in variable `GH_API_SAFE_USE_READ_TOKEN` (default `0`) is `1` and `is_read=1`, it tries `gh_api_safe_job_token_read` once before its existing loop.
  - On success it sets `GH_API_SAFE_OUTPUT` and returns 0.
  - Otherwise it runs today's PAT loop unchanged.

  Callers set the variable inline, as in the existing `GH_API_SAFE_QUIET_STDERR=1 gh_api_safe` idiom, so only the per-tick call sites opt in.

- **Add `gh_api_safe_quiet_print_read`.** It is a thin wrapper that runs `GH_API_SAFE_USE_READ_TOKEN=1 gh_api_safe_quiet_print "$@"`. Check the name is unused first.

### 3. Per-tick call sites (reads only; dispatch, comment, label, delete and merge calls stay unchanged)

- **`scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh`** (it loads `gh_helpers.sh` at line 216):
  - the idle-wait loop read (line ~1726, `…/runs?per_page=30`);
  - the gate poll read (line ~1774, `…/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&per_page=50`).

  Both change from `gh_retry gh api …` to `gh_retry gh_read --same-repo-only api …`. The one-off `before_gate_ids` read and `gh workflow run` stay as they are.

- **`scripts/workflow_failure_heal_queue.sh`** (it loads `gh_helpers.sh` at line 65), wait loop:
  - the comments listing (line ~245, `--method GET --paginate --slurp`);
  - the holder-run read (line ~283).

  Both become `gh_retry gh_read --same-repo-only api --method GET …`. The ticket POST and stale DELETE stay on `gh_retry gh api`.

- **`scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh`:** the registration poll (line ~255) and the completion poll (line ~345) change from `gh_api_safe_quiet_print` to `gh_api_safe_quiet_print_read`. The one-off snapshot read and the dispatch stay as they are.
